title.name: Stone by Stone
title.subtitle: The town and palace of Olite
menu.easy.note: More cards, fewer fires and a patient king. No turn limit.
menu.normal.note: Finish the works by turn 30 without losing the king's trust.
intro.1: Navarre, about 650 years ago. Olite is a small town among wheatfields and vineyards.
intro.2: King Charles III, known as the Noble, likes Olite so much that he wants to live there.
intro.3: But first, the town: bread for everyone, and new walls. Start stone by stone!
outro.1: Over the years, Olite gained one of the richest palaces of its time in Europe: towers, hanging gardens and even lions.
outro.2: The Royal Palace of Olite still stands. You can visit it and climb its towers!

fact.charles: Charles III the Noble ruled Navarre from 1387 to 1425 and made Olite one of his favourite homes.
fact.leonor: Queen Leonor of Trastámara, Charles III's wife, also lived in the palace at Olite.
fact.gardens: The palace is said to have had hanging gardens, with trees planted high on its walls.
fact.lions: The king kept exotic animals at Olite: lions, camels and faraway birds are mentioned.
fact.wine: Olite's wine was so prized that it was served at court and sold far away.
fact.craftspeople: Christian, Jewish and Mudéjar craftspeople from Navarre and other kingdoms worked on the palace.
fact.fire: In 1813, in the war against Napoleon, the palace was burned so the French could not use it.
fact.restoration: The palace was restored in the 20th century; today you can visit and climb its towers.

card.labourer.name: Labourer
card.labourer.history: Labourers carried stone, dug trenches and mixed the lime.
card.mason.name: Stonemason
card.mason.history: Masons cut the stone; some carved their mark on the blocks.
card.carpenter.name: Carpenter
card.carpenter.history: Carpenters made beams, gates, scaffolds and carts.
card.stone.name: Stone
card.stone.history: Stone came from nearby quarries in ox carts.
card.timber.name: Timber
card.timber.history: Some timber came down from the Pyrenees on log rafts, by river.
card.lime.name: Lime
card.lime.history: Lime was made by burning limestone in kilns; mixed with sand it made mortar.
card.permit.name: Royal charter
card.permit.text: The king's leave for big works.
card.permit.history: Navarre's kings granted towns like Olite charters for their walls and markets.
card.gift.name: Wine for the king
card.gift.text: Give it: +3 favour. Or keep it for a request.
card.gift.history: Olite's wine was served at the royal table.
card.baker.name: Baker
card.baker.text: On the map: +3 bread to its block, +1 to the blocks around. Can move.
card.baker.history: Bread was the main food; towns had bakers and baking ovens.
card.oven.name: Bread oven
card.oven.text: On an empty lot: +2 bread to its block and all around it. Fixed.
card.oven.history: Many towns had shared ovens where people took their bread to bake.
card.firewatch.name: Fire watch
card.firewatch.text: On the map: puts out fires beside it and stops them starting. Can move.
card.firewatch.history: With wooden houses packed close, one fire could sweep a whole street.
card.buckets.name: Bucket chain
card.buckets.history: Against fire, neighbours formed chains passing buckets of water.
project.market.name: Market
project.market.history: The market sold wine, grain, cloth and tools.
project.well.name: Well
project.well.text: On a lot: nothing near it catches fire. You can build several.
project.well.history: Wells and cisterns gave water to drink and to fight fires.
project.wall_n.name: North wall
project.wall_n.history: Olite was ringed by walls; parts of them can still be seen.
project.wall_e.name: East wall
project.wall_e.history: The walls protected the town and marked where it began.
project.wall_s.name: South wall
project.wall_s.text: A stretch of the walls. Then: the gate.
project.wall_s.history: Raising a wall took masons, labourers and a lot of lime.
project.gate.name: Town gate
project.gate.history: Goods, travellers and the king's court came in through the town gates.
